answers.solution: To a common man, a problem is anything that disturbs his peace of mind (his 'equilibrium') because it stops him from achieving something he wants. It can also be anything that creates a difficulty for him or makes his situation more complicated.
answers.finalAnswer: Anything that disturbs his balance because it stops him from getting what he wants, or anything that makes things difficult or more complicated for him.

answers.solution: For someone who loves to face problems, a problem is not a trouble but an opportunity to test himself. Such people believe that these situations teach them many lessons of life and finally help them become better versions of themselves.

answers.solution: Problems are a part of every person's life, from a student to a Prime Minister, and they differ in seriousness from person to person. Many of them are created by us and can be avoided through good habits such as managing time, respecting elders, being kind and caring for nature. The problems that remain should not be feared; like the people mentioned at the end of the passage, we can treat them as opportunities to learn and become better.
answers.finalAnswer: Problems are a part of everyone's life; many are of our own making and can be avoided by good habits, and the rest can be faced as opportunities to learn and grow.

The Editor
The Times of India
New Delhi

Subject: Being ready for a future pandemic

Sir,

Through your newspaper, I wish to suggest how our nation can deal with another pandemic in future.

COVID-19 caught us unprepared. First, every district must have well-equipped hospitals with enough beds, oxygen and trained staff. Second, people should follow good habits even in normal times: washing hands, wearing masks in crowds and eating healthy food. Third, schools and offices must be ready to shift online quickly, so that learning and work do not stop. Fourth, the government should keep a store of medicines and vaccines and share correct information, so that rumours do not spread panic. Finally, we must help the poor and the elderly, who suffer most in such times.

If we prepare now, we can face the next pandemic with courage.

Yours faithfully,
Arjun Singh

Title: Kinds of Students

Students are usually grouped as good, naughty and weak. Good students are intelligent, obedient, punctual and modest. Naughty students, though often clever, disturb the class, quarrel and may even steal. Weak students do poorly in exams because they do not understand their lessons, owing to a poor foundation or a lack of confidence, motivation or guidance. Teachers and parents must work together to find the cause, motivate such students, clear their doubts and help them set realistic goals.

My Favourite Dream

When night comes down and stars appear,
I close my eyes and lose my fear.
A dream comes softly, bright and clear,
The one I love throughout the year.

I wear a cadet's uniform with pride,
My friends are marching by my side.
The drums are beating, loud and wide,
And flags are waving far and wide.

I fly a jet above the land,
The mountains look like grains of sand.
I guard my country, firm I stand,
With courage strong and steady hand.

Then morning comes, the dream must end,
But I will work, my dream to tend.
On hard work only I depend,
To make my dream come true, my friend.

Effect of the Pandemic on the Education of School-going Children
By Arjun Singh, Class VII

In March 2020, schools across India suddenly shut their gates because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Classrooms fell silent, and for nearly two years children studied from home. This changed school education in many ways.

The biggest change was online learning. Classes moved to mobile phones and laptops. Students learnt to use video calls, online tests and digital notes. Many children became good at using technology, and some discovered they could learn on their own.

However, the harm was greater. Millions of children in villages and poor families had no smartphone or internet connection, so they could not attend classes at all. Many fell behind, and some left school to help their families earn money. Even those who studied online found it hard to concentrate for hours in front of a small screen. Long screen time caused headaches, eye strain and poor sleep.

Children also missed the joys of school life: playing with friends, sports, assemblies and talking face to face with teachers. Many felt lonely, bored or anxious. Teachers say that young children lost basic reading and writing skills, and older students forgot much of what they had learnt.

Now that schools have reopened, we must help children catch up. Extra classes, remedial teaching and counselling can fill the gaps. The government should also make sure every child has access to digital devices, so that no child is left behind if schools ever have to close again.

The pandemic taught us that a school is not only a place to study, but also a place to grow.

Best Friends Forever

Every evening, little Riya and her golden dog Bruno walked down the shady path behind their house. Tall ferns grew on both sides, and the trees whispered in the breeze. Bruno wagged his fluffy tail and never left Riya's side.

One evening Riya walked too far and the sky grew dark. She could not find the way back and began to cry. Bruno licked her hand, sniffed the ground and gently pulled at her sleeve. Riya held on to his soft fur and followed him.

Step by step, Bruno led her along the path until the lights of her house appeared. Her worried parents ran out and hugged her tightly. That night Riya gave Bruno an extra biscuit and whispered, 'You are my best friend forever.'

(a) are: 'a number of' means many, so the verb is plural.
(b) is: 'dal and rice' is one dish.
(c) has: 'sugar' is uncountable.
(d) was: 'income' is uncountable.
(e) are: 'police' always takes a plural verb.
(f) are: with 'neither ... nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'the two students'.
(g) likes: the subject is 'one'.
(h) were: an imaginary condition takes 'were'.
(i) are: two subjects joined by 'and'.
(j) is: with 'as well as' the verb agrees with the first subject, 'Aman'.
answers.finalAnswer: are; is; has; was; are; are; likes; were; are; is
